theme: open-collaboration restructure: entry point, cards, registry split, CLI, skills
question: Can the repository be restructured so that many people and agents contribute in parallel from one entry point, without moving or losing any existing evidence?
outcome: AGENTS.md rewritten as a single entry point with every earlier rule and the data-first rule; README rewritten for people with dated sections moved verbatim to knowledge/TIMELINE.md (all 62 old links retained); registry split into 165 per-entry files with status_class and area, regenerated registry.json field-equal to the original; 33 finding cards, 38 general question cards, generated knowledge/MAP.md, tools/kb.py (search, show, list, next, new, build, check), seven skills, four issue forms and llms.txt. kb.py check passes with 0 errors; a second build changes nothing. Performed by Codex CLI (GPT-6.1-Sol, xhigh) from a written prompt; reviewed by the coordinator.
challenge: Uncommitted edits from earlier sessions in shared files; parallel contributors writing cards and data files; 112 free-text statuses needing judged classes; the legacy verifier rejects the newly authorised data/MANIFEST.json and reports 25 older missing targets.
remedy: Owned-path list and no-move rule in the prompt; baseline hashes of 18,871 files; per-entry preservation check; hand classification recorded in STATUS-MAPPING.md; verification outputs kept in the package.
retry_when: The contributor model changes (for example a licence or CI decision), or kb.py check reports drift.
